name: Jeff Hurd

summary.text: Jeff Hurd is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Colorado's 3rd Congressional District, in office since January 2025.
He is an attorney who worked at the Grand Junction Area Chamber of Commerce, clerked for 10th Circuit Judge Timothy Tymkovich, and co-owned a law firm before his election.
He was born in Grand Junction, Colorado, in 1979.

experience.text: Bachelor's degree in liberal studies (classical literature and philosophy), University of Notre Dame
J.D., University of Denver Sturm College of Law, 2008; LL.M., Columbia Law School, 2010
Law clerk, U.S. Court of Appeals for the 10th Circuit, Judge Timothy Tymkovich
Co-owner of a law firm; previously worked at the Grand Junction Area Chamber of Commerce
U.S. House, Colorado's 3rd Congressional District, January 2025-present; chair, Indian and Insular Affairs Subcommittee, House Natural Resources Committee

record.detail: Voted Yea, one of six Republicans to join Democrats. Passed 219-211.

record.title: Joint statement with Rep. Joe Neguse on removal of public lands sell-off from the 2025 budget reconciliation bill
record.detail: Issued a joint statement with Rep. Neguse after the Senate parliamentarian removed public-lands-sale provisions from the reconciliation bill, after the two worked to strip a related land-sale amendment from the House-passed text.

record.title: Crystal Reservoir land transfer
record.detail: According to Hurd, he introduced legislation transferring the federally owned Crystal Reservoir and surrounding acreage to the City of Ouray to let the community restore a local water resource.

positions.source_title: Roll Call 190, H.R. 1 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act), motion to concur in Senate amendment
positions.quote: Representative Hurd (CO) of Republican from Colorado Voted Aye
positions.note: Later said of the bill, "I supported the legislation while recognizing that it was not perfect" (Aspen Times, Oct. 7, 2026).

positions.note: Voted for the Laken Riley Act, which expanded mandatory detention of certain noncitizens and enforcement-related authorities.

positions.quote: Representative Hurd (CO) of Republican from Colorado Voted Yea
positions.note: Voted for the bill barring transgender girls and women from female school sports teams.

positions.source_title: Roll Call 65, H.J.Res. 72, terminating the national emergency underlying tariffs on Canada
positions.quote: Representative Hurd (CO) of Republican from Colorado Voted Yea
positions.note: One of six Republicans who voted to end the Canada tariff emergency; voting Yea is against keeping the tariffs.

positions.source_title: Colorado Representatives Jeff Hurd and Joe Neguse Statement on Removal of Public Lands Sell Off from Budget Reconciliation Bill
positions.quote: Republican or Democrat—representing red, purple, or blue districts—one sentiment continues to ring true: public lands are not for sale.
positions.note: Joint statement with Rep. Joe Neguse; the two also worked to strip a House-passed land-sale amendment. In an October 2026 Aspen Times Q&A he gave a more qualified version: "I do not support wholesale sales of our public lands," while saying narrowly tailored, locally driven land conveyances can make sense.

positions.source_title: Colorado U.S. House District 3 candidate Q&A (The Denver Post)
positions.quote: Rural Coloradans often have fewer health care options and higher costs. I worked across the aisle and voted to extend enhanced premium tax credits while Congress pursues lasting reforms.
positions.note: Coded as mixed: he also supports Medicaid work requirements for able-bodied adults (Aspen Times Q&A, October 7, 2026) and voted for H.R. 1, which reduced Medicaid spending.

positions.source_title: Congressman Hurd speaks at Pro-Life rally
positions.quote: I have my pro-life views, but I understand others disagree and I think that exchange of ideas and sharing perspectives is something important in our society
positions.note: Made at a Mesa County Right to Life rally. He has separately been reported (politiquote.gigafact.org, citing a Sept. 30, 2024 debate) as saying "I'm pro life with exceptions" and that he would not vote for a federal abortion ban, leaving the issue to states.

positions.source_title: Where Jeff Hurd and Dwayne Romero stand on the top issues in Colorado's 3rd Congressional District race
positions.quote: He is a proponent of multiple energy sources such as carbon-based, renewable, geothermal, and nuclear energy. He said he would not like to see any energy sources taken off the table.
positions.note: Answering a Colorado Sun question on whether the U.S. should stop using carbon-emitting energy sources; he favors an all-of-the-above mix rather than speeding a shift off fossil fuels, and separately supports 'responsible' oil and gas development on federal lands in the same article.
